roles.description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. Summer Internship Our Summer Internship is designed for students leading into their final year of university, who want to gain real life work experience in a fast past, exciting and professional environment. As a Summer Intern, you will participate in onboarding with the UR team that will set you up for success in your role. You will also benefit from professional development sessions, networking, and social events provided by the Internship Program. The program takes place from June – August 2027 (10-week program). Your Role As a Talent Growth & Inclusion intern, you'll own a meaningful piece of an enterprise-level Talent Management project - spanning career development, performance, learning, inclusion, or leadership development. You'll work directly with the Talent Growth & Inclusion team, People Partners, and subject matter experts. You'll be expected to ask good questions, form a point of view, and present it - not just execute a task list. What you'll do Take a loosely defined problem and turn it into a clear plan: what you're solving, what you need to know, and how you'll get there. Research, synthesize, and structure complex information into something a busy executive can act on. Build presentation-ready deliverables - documents, frameworks, decks, or tools - that hold up without heavy editing. Communicate proactively: flag blockers early, surface what you've learned, and tell us when your thinking has changed. Present your work and recommendations to the team, and to People & Culture stakeholders. What we're looking for Critical thinking. You don't stop at the first answer. You ask why, look for what's missing, and can explain the reasoning behind your recommendation — not just the recommendation. Creative problem solving. You're comfortable when there's no template. You generate options, weigh trade-offs, and try a different angle when the first one stalls. Communication, written and verbal. You write clearly and concisely for the reader in front of you. You speak up in meetings, ask the question you're not sure you should ask, and keep people informed without being chased. You own the outcome, not just the effort. You meet commitments, tell us early when you can't, incorporate feedback the first time, and check your own work before it reaches someone else's desk. How we work with AI We use AI at Veeam every day, and we want you to use it too. But we're specific about how. AI is a tool for extending your thinking — pressure-testing an idea, accelerating research, drafting a starting point, checking your logic. It is not a substitute for it. Interns who thrive here use AI to get further, faster, and can still explain every choice in their work, defend it under questioning, and tell you what the model got wrong. Work that's been outsourced to a model shows immediately, and it doesn't meet our bar. If you're curious about applying AI to make career, learning, and performance experiences more personalized and scalable, you'll have room to run with that here. Requirements Rising junior or senior pursuing a bachelor's degree, or a graduate student, at an accredited college or university — studying Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business, Psychology, Education, or a related field Strong interest in talent development, career growth, performance, learning programs, leadership development, organizational effectiveness, or change management Demonstrated ability to structure and communicate complex information clearly in writing Comfortable working with data, templates, and structured frameworks — and comfortable when none exist yet Organized and detail-oriented; able to track tasks, feedback, and deliverables across multiple workstreams Fluent with Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and AI-enabled tools, with a willingness to learn new technologies Collaborative across functions and levels; curious, proactive, and eager to learn Nice to have: prior internship, project, or coursework related to HR, learning programs, data analysis, or change initiatives Benefits As a paid intern at Veeam, you’ll receive: Paid Company Holidays during your internship Tech Stipend to help set up your workspace 8 Hours of Paid Volunteer Time through our Veeam Cares Program Personal and Professional Development through our Internship Program We’re committed to providing a supportive and rewarding internship experience. The pay range posted is an hourly rate of base pay. When making an offer of employment, Veeam will take into consideration the candidate’s expectations, experience, education, scope of responsibility for the role, and the current market demands. United States of America Intern Pay Range $20- $25 USD Veeam Software is an equal opportunity employer and does not tolerate discrimination in any form on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, citizenship, disability, veteran status or any other classification protected by federal, state or local law. roles.title: UX Research Intern (Summer 2027)
roles.description: At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Lyft is seeking a Mixed Methods User Experience Research Intern to join our team, which aspires to elevate the user experience for our drivers and riders across 300+ cities nationwide. You will conduct research studies, as well as participate in studies alongside more senior researchers from which you’ll gain strong mentorship. You will partner with Design, Product Management, Analytics, and Engineering in order to derive deep insights about our users’ behaviors and attitudes, and communicate results and actionable recommendations across the company. Interns contribute to user-facing products, working side-by-side with top User Experience Research team members in the industry while having autonomy from the get-go. Lyft fosters a collaborative environment in the office, so there's always a sharp mind eager to hear about your next idea. So what's yours? Responsibilities: Design and conduct studies across key Lyft product areas -- independently and in conjunction with more senior researchers. You will utilize methods such as ethnographic & field research, diary studies, surveys, user/usability testing (remote and in-person), guerrilla research, and any other methods you find impactful Review, analyze, and communicate qualitative and/or quantitative data to generate tactical and strategic insights, as well as actionable recommendations which drive product innovation and design improvements for users Experience: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree in Human-Computer Interaction, Anthropology, Design, Psychology, Cognitive Science, or a related field from a university in Canada with a graduation date between December 2027 and Summer 2028 (required) Available during Summer 2027 for an internship in Toronto Extraordinary organizational skills and meticulous eye for detail Strong listening and analytical skills; proactive troubleshooter Team player with excellent written & verbal communication skills Enthusiasm for a collaborative, highly energetic, fun and fast-paced environment Experience as a researcher and/or research coordinator for qualitative research studies or school-based research projects, including usability/user testing, surveys, field research, or user interviews Bonus Points: Research experience with mobile technology Experience conducting qualitative research in applied research settings, ideally within a Product organization Experience designing surveys and experimental research, and analyzing large datasets using appropriate statistical methods Experience using Qualtrics or SurveyMonkey Experience cleaning, handling, and transforming data in Microsoft Excel and/or Google Sheets Experience with SQL, R, and/or other data analysis software (e.g., SPSS) Experience with research participant recruitment and management practices Design thinking, visual communication, information design, or wireframing skills Benefits: Mental health benefits In addition to holidays, interns receive 2 days paid time off and 3 days sick time off Subsidized commuter benefits and Lyft ride credits Lyft is committed to creating an inclusive workforce that fosters belonging. Lyft believes that every person has a right to equal employment opportunities without discrimination because of race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, family status, disability, pardoned record of offences, or any other basis protected by applicable law or by Company policy. Lyft also strives for a healthy and safe workplace and strictly prohibits harassment of any kind. Accommodation for persons with disabilities will be provided upon request in accordance with applicable law during the application and hiring process. Please contact your recruiter if you wish to make such a request. Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule — Team Members will be expected to work in the office at least 3 days per week, including on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. roles.title: ATR – Internship 2027 - HRBP
roles.description: Job Description: Envie de rejoindre l'aventure ATR ? Une offre de stage RH vient de s'ouvrir sur notre site à Saint Martin / Blagnac ! En 2025, ATR est labellisée Happy Trainees. 94.3% des étudiants recommandent notre entreprise à l’issue de leur alternance ou de leur stage. Ce que nous allons faire ensemble : Être stagiaire chez ATR, c’est être intégré au sein d’une équipe comme un membre à part entière avec un véritable périmètre d’intervention et des responsabilités. Votre mission Au sein de l'équipe Ressources Humaines, en FAL (Final Assembly Line), vous participerez à l'accompagnement des transformations humaines et organisationnelles des chaînes d'assemblage, dans un contexte d'évolution des métiers, des modes de travail et des attentes des salariés. Vous contribuerez à des projets à fort impact visant à adapter les pratiques RH et managériales aux nouveaux enjeux de l'industrie, tout en accompagnant au quotidien les HR Business Partners sur leurs activités opérationnelles. Vos principales missions Accompagnement du changement et expérience collaborateur Réaliser des diagnostics et analyses des attentes des différentes populations (nouvelles générations, femmes dans l'industrie, salariés expérimentés, etc.). Contribuer aux réflexions autour de l'amélioration de la Qualité de Vie et des Conditions de Travail (QVCT). Accompagner les évolutions organisationnelles et les nouvelles pratiques issues des transformations de l'entreprise. Participer aux travaux sur les parcours professionnels, les mobilités et les perspectives de carrière en production. Animer ou coanimer des groupes de travail, ateliers participatifs et tables rondes avec les salariés et les managers. Préparer des supports de communication, kits managers et actions de sensibilisation. Contribuer à la conception de Team Talks et d'événements thématiques autour de sujets tels que la diversité, l'inclusion et la lutte contre les discriminations. Participer à la mesure de l'impact des actions mises en œuvre et proposer des plans d'amélioration. Support RH opérationnel aux HR Business Partners En parallèle de ces projets de transformation, vous accompagnerez les HRBP dans leurs activités quotidiennes : Suivi des effectifs et des indicateurs RH, Réalisation d'analyses et de reporting RH. Participation aux campagnes RH : People Tempo (Définition des objectifs 2027, Revues de Performance 2026, Politique salariale 2027, People Reviews) Préparation et suivi des contrats et avenants. Interface avec les équipes Administration du Personnel et Paie. Participation à certaines activités de relations sociales. Appui aux managers sur des sujets RH de premier niveau. Ce stage est fait pour vous : Formation en Ressources Humaines, Psychologie du Travail, Sociologie des Organisations. Vous recherchez un stage de fin d'études de 6 mois. Vous êtes intéressé(e) par les enjeux humains liés aux transformations des organisations. Vous appréciez le travail de terrain et les échanges avec des populations opérationnelles. Vous disposez d'excellentes capacités d'analyse, de rigueur, de pro-activité, de communication et de synthèse. Vous êtes à l'aise dans l'animation d'ateliers et dans la conduite de projets. Vous maîtrisez Excel et PowerPoint. La maîtrise de l'anglais est un plus. Ce que nous vous offrons Un stage à forte valeur ajoutée au cœur des enjeux de transformation d'un environnement industriel. Une exposition à la fois stratégique et opérationnelle des Ressources Humaines. Des missions variées associant conduite du changement, communication, développement RH et support aux HRBP. Une expérience de terrain au contact des managers et des équipes de production. L'opportunité de contribuer directement à l'évolution de l'expérience collaborateur dans l'industrie de demain. Une équipe HRBP dynamique qui met l'humain au centre de son quotidien. Calendrier Démarrage à partir de Janvier 2027 Durée 6 mois Comment se passe le processus de recrutement ? Le processus de recrutement se passe en deux étapes après la réception de votre candidature : Analyse des CV Entretien technique Manager : Le responsable du stage Fanny vous contactera pour un entretien de recrutement Want to join the ATR adventure? An internship opportunity has just opened on our site in St Martin / Blagnac ! In 2025, ATR has been awarded the Happy Trainees label. 94.3% of students recommend our company after their work-study or internship. What we will do together: Being an apprentice at ATR means being integrated into a team as a full member with a real scope of intervention and responsibilities. You will have the opportunity to learn and develop your skills and experience within a market leading company! Detailed description of the mission Within the Human Resources team supporting the Final Assembly Line (FAL), you will contribute to the human and organizational transformation of assembly line operations in a context marked by evolving jobs, ways of working, and employees expectations. You will be involved in high-impact projects aimed at adapting HR and management practices to meet the emerging challenges of the industrial environment, while also supporting HR Business Partners in their day-to-day operational activities. Main Responsibilities 1. Change Management and Employee Experience (Main Assignment) You will contribute to the design and deployment of initiatives aimed at supporting the transformation of production organizations by: Conducting assessments and analyses of the expectations and needs of various employee populations (new generations, women in industry, experienced employees, etc.). Contributing to initiatives focused on improving Quality of Work Life and Working Conditions (QWL/WLC). Supporting organizational changes and the adoption of new practices resulting from business transformations. Participating in projects related to career paths, internal mobility, and career development opportunities within production. Facilitating or co-facilitating working groups, participative workshops, and roundtable discussions with employees and managers. Preparing communication materials, manager toolkits, and awareness-raising initiatives. Contributing to the design of Team Talks and thematic events covering topics such as diversity, inclusion, and the prevention of discrimination. Supporting the measurement of the impact of implemented actions and recommending continuous improvement plans. 2. Operational HR Support to HR Business Partners Alongside these transformation projects, you will support HR Business Partners in their day-to-day activities, including: Monitoring workforce data and HR KPIs, and producing HR analyses and reports. Supporting key HR cycles and campaigns, including People Tempo (2027 Goal Setting, 2026 Performance Reviews, 2027 Compensation Review, and People Reviews). Preparing and following up on employment contracts and contractual amendments. Acting as an interface with Payroll and Personnel Administration teams. Providing first-level HR support and guidance to managers. This internship is designed for you Master's degree or equivalent in Human Resources, Occupational Psychology, or Organizational Sociology. You are looking for a 6 ‑ month end-of-studies internship. You have a strong interest in the people-related challenges associated with organizational transformation. You enjoy working closely with operational teams and interacting with employees in industrial environments. You possess excellent analytical, organizational, communication, and synthesis skills, combined with a proactive mindset. You are comfortable facilitating workshops and contributing to project management activities. You are proficient in Excel and PowerPoint. A high-impact internship at the heart of transformation initiatives in a dynamic industrial environment. Exposure to both the strategic and operational dimensions of Human Resources. Diverse assignments combining change management, communication, talent and HR development, and support to HR Business Partners. An experience in Production, working alongside managers and production teams. A unique opportunity to contribute directly to shaping the employee experience in the industry of tomorrow. roles.title: Australia Community Engagement Internship
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Australia Team Zipline is building its presence in Australia, and we are looking for an exceptional student or recent graduate to join the team as a part-time Australia Expansion Fellow. The Australia team is responsible for developing the partnerships, market strategy and operations required to bring Zipline’s autonomous logistics system to communities across the country. This means working at the intersection of business, government, technology and community to understand where Zipline can have the greatest impact and what it will take to get there. The Role As an Australia Expansion Fellow, you will work directly with Zipline’s Head of Australia on our community engagement strategy. This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend time with our local leadership out in the community, meeting residents, businesses and community organisations, listening to their perspectives and ensuring questions and concerns are addressed. You will help translate our exciting but unfamiliar technology into clear, credible and locally relevant conversations. roles.title: Behavioral Health Intern
roles.description: SUMMARY: Under the direction of Clinical Manager (Inpatient)/Program Director (Partial/Residential), the Behavioral Health Intern (BHI) is responsible for providing care and safety to children and adolescents as a member of the interdisciplinary treatment team. The BHI is responsible for input into the formulation of the day-to-day schedule and structure of a therapeutic milieu and the implementation, observation, and documentation of this program under the direction of the program/shift lead. Brown University Health employees are expected to successfully role model the organization's values of Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence as these values guide our everyday actions with patients, customers and one another. In addition to our values, all employees are expected to demonstrate the core Success Factors which tell us how we work together and how we get things done. The core Success Factors include: Instill Trust and Value Differences Patient and Community Focus and Collaborate RESPONSIBILITIES: Brown University Health employees are expected to successfully role model the organization’s values of Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence as these guide our everyday actions with patients, customers and one another. A. Participates in maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment. Actively engages with assigned children throughout shift. Participates in the development and operationalization of the milieu care plan for assigned patients according to established department and unit-based procedure/policy. Maintains and documents level of patient observation as ordered by the physician. Provides support to visiting parents as well as information according to treatment team request. Supervises assigned children in daily routines and actively assists with activities of daily living and basic hygiene needs. Identifies, reports, and resolves potentialctual problems on the unit. Demonstrates appropriate critical incident follow-up skills by timely verbal reporting to charge RN or Shift Leader and documentation in medical record. Completes other documentation (i.e., incident reports, intakes, etc. as applicable). Participates in event debriefings. Carries out daily assignment and reports back prior to change of shift. Intervenes in disruptive milieu or destructive to self/other patient situations providing timely therapeutic intervention(s) to children in distress. Maintains appropriate boundaries. B. Adheres to Hospital, Departmental, and Program policies and procedures. C. Actively participates in the patient care planning process under the direction of the primary/charge RN or Shift Lead. Works to support initial therapeutic alliance with patient and family on admission. Assists with the separation process and performs other duties necessary to provide a smooth transition to the hospital environment. Within the 8-hour shift, documents objective observations within a shift note and shares observations with assigned RN/Shift Lead. Reviews milieu care plan and problem list on a daily basis and suggests revisions based on observations. Communicates individual patient milieu care plans in an ongoing manner to other unit staff including liaison with other interdisciplinary treatment providers. Actively participates in treatment team, rounds, patient-specific discussions, and hand-off shift report, as assigned. Accurately documents significant patient/family observations/milieu care on the Kardex and medical records in a timely fashion. Offers information and knowledge acquired through experience to other staff via formal/ informal staff development forums. Is able to adapt care to meet needs of various childrendolescents. D. Supports and contributes to the development of care plans/behavioral management. Assists and teaches patients in activities of daily living and personal hygiene based upon patient’s abilities. Co-leads community meeting/milieu meeting/social skill group. Co-leads other program specific groups such as activity or recreation. Demonstrates ability to set consistent and supportive therapeutic limits within guidelines of hospital, unit, and department standards. Follows behavioral programs specific to the needs of the patient in collaboration with the assigned RN/Shift Lead and treatment team. Organizes unit activities. Coordinates, supervises and actively participates in children’s activities such as physical &social development activities. Arranges for transportation of materials if required. Participates in teaching visits/family and parent training as assigned. Consistently models to patient/families appropriate and therapeutic interpersonal staff/patient interactions. Co-leads therapy groups with a clinician. Supports and actively participates in recreation therapy programs. Handles crisis situations in a safe, effective manner, utilizing the least restrictive, safe patient care alternative. Takes the initiative to seek formalnformal supervision, incorporating suggestions for improvement/changes in job performance. Performs other related duties as required, assigned, or directed by Charge RN/shift lead. While an individual is hired to work on a particular program, they may at times be asked to perform comparable duties in other clinical settings throughout the hospital system as program needs arise. BASIC KNOWLEDGE: Current certification in Basic Life Support through the American Heart Association. Current matriculation in an accredited Bachelor of Arts (BA) or Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in human services with completed coursework in psychology and social sciences is preferred.Candidates in an Associate’s Degree (AD) program may be considered. Demonstrated knowledge and skills necessary to provide care to patients throughout the life span with consideration of aging processes human development stages and cultural patterns in each step of the care process. Bradley Hospital Safety Care Specialist Certification: *This will be provided to BHIs upon orientation Employees in this position work in a psychiatric setting under stressful conditions associated with care of psychiatrically impaired, aggressive, and sometimes, self-injurious individuals. Employees are expected to utilize de-escalation techniques taught by Bradley Hospital to minimize need for physical intervention. They must have the ability to remain calm during a crisis situation as evidenced by the ability to make quick rational decisions and prioritize immediate patient care needs to maintain a therapeutic environment and ensure safety. Employees in this position must also be able to participate in the physical management of patients which can include, but is not limited to, awareness and demonstration of safe body positioning at all times, awareness and coordination to block and deflect possible aggression, and the ability to physically hold struggling patients, using approved methods only, to maintain safety for extended periods of time. Specifically, such employees must be able to: lift up to fifty pounds; reach with their hands and arms; grasp and hold with their hands; bend/squat/kneel without limitation, and physically escort patients who may become combative for short distances. Position requires occasional running for short distances, and frequent standing, walking, and sitting. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: EXPERIENCE: Current matriculation in an accredited Bachelor of Arts (BA) or Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in human services with completed coursework in psychology and social sciences is preferred INDEPENDENT ACTION: Works under the supervision of the Registered Nurse or Program Supervisor within the scope of Hospital and department policies and procedures. Refers specific complex problems to supervisor where clarification of Program policies and procedures may be required. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY: None Pay Range: $18.00-$27.13 EEO Statement: Brown University Health is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and maintaining a work environment free from all forms of unlawful discrimination and harassment. roles.title: Business Development Management Intern - 2027
roles.description: Do you want to help advance AI by connecting breakthrough technology with developers, researchers, startups, and industry leaders across China? NVIDIA’s Worldwide Field Operations China team is looking for a Business Development Intern to help us grow strategic accounts and strengthen the AI developer ecosystem. Together, we work with developers, researchers, startups, independent software vendors, and customers across industries including internet services, cloud computing, and IoT. In this internship, you will gain hands-on experience in ecosystem development, go-to-market execution, and strategic business development. We will help you build knowledge of NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform—from the data center to the edge—while you collaborate with teams across Business Development, Solutions Architecture, Software and Hardware Engineering, Product, Marketing, and Sales. What You’ll Be Doing: Support strategic account and partnership initiatives by coordinating research, materials, and follow-up activities across teams. Build an understanding of NVIDIA’s AIPS sales motion by working closely with Solutions Architecture and DevTech teams to accelerate library integration and drive adoption. Engage with developers, researchers, software partners, and technology decision-makers to gain a deeper understanding of customer workloads and turn your findings into practical insights. Prepare customer and partner profiles, meeting materials, internal updates, and recommendations that help our teams make informed decisions. Collect and organize customer feedback, feature requests, and market requirements for relevant product and technical teams. Coordinate technical meetups, research conferences, community activities, and industry events, including outreach, attendee tracking, and post-event reporting. Work with account managers and business development teams on projects that support NVIDIA’s strategic accounts and broader AI ecosystem. What We Need to See: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Marketing, or a related field. An interest in AI, machine learning, accelerated computing, cloud technologies, or developer ecosystems, along with a willingness to keep learning. The ability to research unfamiliar topics, organize information, identify useful insights, and communicate clear recommendations. Clear written and verbal communication skills in both Chinese and English. Experience using productivity and collaboration tools, with an openness to learning new AI-enabled tools. The ability to take ownership of defined assignments, ask thoughtful questions, and work well with people from different functions. Availability to meet the internship schedule agreed upon with the team. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Coursework, projects, internships, student organizations, or event experience related to AI, cloud computing, startups, developer communities, or business development. Examples of using research or data to identify trends, explain an opportunity, or recommend an action. Experience supporting events, communities, outreach programs, or cross-functional projects. Curiosity about how AI technology creates customer value and business impact. A learning-oriented approach, thoughtful follow-through, and a willingness to contribute new ideas. You will have opportunities to learn from experienced business and technical teams, understand how NVIDIA brings AI solutions to market, and contribute to projects involving customers and ecosystem partners. You will also gain exposure to NVIDIA technologies, developer programs, and real-world applications of accelerated computing. We are building an environment where people can learn, contribute, and do their best work together. Join us and help shape how AI reaches developers, businesses, and communities across China! NVIDIA is committed to fostering a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to legally protected characteristics. Reasonable accommodations are available to candidates who need assistance during the application or interview process.

roles.title: Change Management Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the NPI Team The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission. About The Role This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity. What You'll Do Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps. Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations. Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field. Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools. Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms. Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data. Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. roles.title: College Intern - HR Information Systems Analyst
roles.description: Overview Ready for takeoff? We are looking for a college intern who will be passionate to work for Envoy Air, the largest regional airline and wholly owned subsidiary of American Airlines. Envoy operates both Embraer E-170 and E-175 aircraft. The regional airline has expanded its network outside of the U.S. to international destinations in Canada, Mexico, and the Caribbean. Our paid 11-week summer internship will not only enhance your studies, but also provide an educational experience you can’t find in the classroom. As an intern, you will learn real world skills while building a professional network of future peers. You will learn the ins and outs of how your team impacts the business day to day and gain an understanding of the commercial aviation business. Responsibilities Interns will function as Financial Analysts in one of the company’s key financial/operational departments (Financial Services, Accounting, Cost Control, Supply Chain or IT Finance). Financial reporting and analysis may cover any part of the business including: Flight Crews, Airport Operations, Maintenance, and Strategic Benchmarking. Each participant will be assigned a mentor and will participate in various training opportunities during the internship. Upon completion of the internship, each intern will have an understanding of the job functions of an analyst as well as an understanding of the commercial aviation business. The Financial Services Intern will partner with other teams where employee HR Data is needed for analysis. Even though not in the HR organization, we are tasked with stewarding this data and it's use within the entire company. The responsibilities of this position include oversight of Organizational Management, Employee Data Reporting, HRIS Configuration and employee-driven projects. Typical job duties include: Assist with planning and coordinating HRIS projects and system improvements, including tracking tasks, timelines, milestones, risks, and action items Support change management activities that help employees and leaders understand and prepare for changes to HR systems, processes, and tools Help develop project and change management materials, including communications, presentations, job aids, training resources, project updates, and other documentation Participate in meetings and working sessions with the HRIS team and business partners to learn about business processes, gather feedback and requirements, and identify opportunities for improvement Assist with testing, implementation, and change readiness activities for HRIS enhancements and new functionality Gain hands-on experience in HRIS, project management, change management, process improvement, and employee technology while supporting cross-functional initiatives The Intern, Envoy Employee Technology will report to the Manager, Envoy HRIS and Reporting Qualifications The ideal candidate must be able to work in a team environment and the ability to prioritize work and projects in order to meet deadlines and objectives. Must be able to work with minimal supervision, report to work regularly and on-time, and be self-motivated. Position Requirements: Minimum age of 18 Enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program in: Management Information Systems, Economics, Organizational Management or Human Resources Management Must be classified as a Junior or Senior upon start of internship 3.25 minimum Grade Point Average Advanced proficiency in MS Office that includes Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook Proficiency in organizational, decision-making and problem-solving skills Ability to present data to all levels of management Must be willing and able to travel Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing Experience sorting, organizing, analyzing and presenting large data sets Experience with problem solving, forecasting, and advanced financial analytical skills Must be able to read, write, fluently speak, and understand the English language Possess the legal right to work in the United States Please note: The description is intended to provide a brief overview of the position. It’s not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, expectations, and skills required of those in this position. Duties and expectations may be subject to change at any time. Envoy Air is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Minorities/Women/Veterans/Disabled. Envoy Air Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of American Airlines Group, provides regional flight service to American Airlines under the American Eagle brand and ground handling services for many American Airlines Group flights. The company was founded in 1998 as American Eagle Airlines, Inc., following the merger of several smaller regional carriers to create one of the largest regional airlines in the world. Envoy is headquartered in Irving, Texas, with hubs in Dallas/Fort Worth, Chicago and Miami, with a large ground handling operation in Los Angeles. roles.title: Community Education Intern
roles.description: ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation. We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government. We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust. ABOUT THE UNIT Public Affairs Division The Public Affairs division engages New Yorkers, informs them about elections, and boosts their participation in the democratic process. We make election information accessible and relevant, increase engagement with underrepresented communities, and cultivate a team that reflects our core values of purpose, curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. The division includes, Marketing and Digital Communications, Community Engagement, Language Access, and Public Relations. Our division’s work includes publishing the citywide Voter Guide, running the official citywide Debates Program, and managing the voter engagement initiative, NYC Votes. Community Engagement Unit The Community Engagement unit works to build partnerships across the city to disseminate voting information, deliver accessible voter education, and conduct direct to voter outreach. Through relationships with community-based organizations as well as on-the-ground voter outreach, this team creates pathways for all New Yorkers to gain trustworthy and accessible information and education around voting and democracy. JOB DESCRIPTION The two Community Education Interns will report to the Youth Engagement Specialist and support civic education and engagement initiatives focused on a youth audience. Interns will help develop and deliver educational programming, support youth-focused events and partnerships, and engage young people in learning about voting and civic participation. Specifically, they will lead workshops on topics related to civic engagement and voter information for audiences of high school and college students both within internal youth programming and with external partners. The role will also support the Community Engagement team in building and maintaining strong internal systems to organize and track partnership development. This includes maintaining team databases, documenting outreach efforts, and supporting data entry. The responsibilities and tasks to be completed in this role include, but are not limited to: Community Education and Outreach - Support the development and delivery of educational programming, both internal and external, for a youth audience. - Independently plan and facilitate NYC Votes workshops in a way that engages the audience. - Represent the CFB and NYC Votes at in-person and virtual events. - Register voters and provide non-partisan election information. - Provide administrative support, such as managing email communication, organizing documents, carrying out internal processes, keeping materials organized, etc. - Identify organizations that work in our priority neighborhoods and serve a youth audience. - Support efforts to build relationships with key stakeholders, such as agencies, community-based organizations, schools, and college campuses. - Willingness to learn about best practices for engaging with priority communities. - Support the development and delivery of educational programming, both internal and external, for a youth audience; this includes leading lesson plans for youth ambassadors, leading workshops with external partners, and supporting curriculum development. - Support data entry efforts, including managing and digitizing physical documents, adding information to appropriate digital folders, and helping manage Excel sheets, etc. ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs) We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. We believe in the power of diverse perspectives and the unique blend of lived experiences, non-traditional education pathways, practical know-how, and a variety of skills and abilities that each candidate brings to the table. If you're ready to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply and be part of our dynamic team. Knowledge - Major in relevant field such as: Political Science, Community Organizing, English, Journalism, Ethnic or Cultural Studies, Social Work, Public Administration, etc. - Understanding or experience with New York City institutions such as libraries, public schools, criminal legal system, CUNY etc. - Interest in New York City politics and/or social justice Skills - Strong organization skills and attention to detail - Proficiency with Microsoft Suite - Strong written and oral communication skills - Strong active listening skills and ability to respond in real time to the concerns and needs of the public Abilities - Willingness to ask questions and learn on the job - Experience with public speaking and community education - Strong facilitation skills, as this intern will be responsible for independently leading workshops and trainings for New Yorkers Other Characteristics - Adaptable and effective collaborator - Ability to learn through receiving and implementing feedback - Willingness to engage in conversation that challenge assumptions and pre-conceived notions of different groups in a way that leads toward culturally competent approach - Ability to work evenings and/or weekends, as needed APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS While completing the application, candidates are invited to provide a cover letter via “attachment” or the “Message to the Hiring Team” field on SmartRecruiters. Please indicate in your cover letter if you’re interested in the community outreach position or the community education position. roles.title: Community Engagement Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Community Engagement Team Zipline's Community Engagement Team plays an important public facing role in Zipline's operations. They are responsible for building and maintaining strong relationships with local government officials, civic organizations, business groups, neighborhoods, and schools. Their work helps individuals and organizations understand the impact of Zipline's service on the community, job creation, and the future of a logistics system that serves all humans equally. The Role Does creating and maintaining important relationships with multiple layers of stakeholders within local communities come naturally to you? Are you an engaging communicator who drives powerful narratives to create excitement and adoption of big and bold ideas? This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about community building, communications, and social impact. You’ll help design and implement strategies to engage our community members, strengthen partnerships, and support outreach initiatives. What You'll Do Assist in planning, promoting, and executing community events, workshops, and virtual meetups. Support the development of content for newsletters, social media, and other communication channels. Respond to community inquiries and engage with members across platforms. Conduct research on community needs, trends, and engagement strategies. Help track engagement metrics and compile reports on community feedback and outcomes. roles.description: Position Title: Community Organizing and Engagement Intern The Agency You’ll Join: In November 2022, New York City voters overwhelmingly approved three ballot proposals that put racial equity and justice at the heart of city government, including the NYC Commission on Racial Equity (NYC CORE). The first of its kind in the nation, the NYC Commission on Racial Equity is an independent 15-member commission responsible for engaging diverse communities to guide and assess the City’s racial equity planning process. NYC CORE provides accountability for New Yorkers, regularly evaluating the City’s progress on its racial requirements and goals. NYC CORE will be composed of diverse New Yorkers with equity expertise and/or relevant lived experience, serving as a conduit to bring historically excluded communities and voices into government decision-making. The Team You’ll Work With: NYC CORE is an independent commission to hold the NYC government accountable to advance racial equity in government operations and to increase community voice in government decision-making. The Chair & Executive Director is jointly appointed by the Mayor and the New York City Council Speaker. Other NYC CORE commissioners are appointed by the Mayor, City Council Speaker, City Comptroller, and Public Advocate. The Commission's staff is responsible for executing the Commission's day-to-day mission and setting its path to success. NYC CORE team takes the vision of the Chair & Executive Director and the Commissioners and translates it into action strategies and plans that implement accountability for racial equity in the city. Like the Commission itself, the Commission’s staff aims to be representative of New Yorkers from all communities and walks of life. Staff bring an accountability mindset to their work, ensuring they collaborate with city agencies and voice public concerns. The Problems You’ll Solve The Community Organizing and Engagement Intern reports directly to the Director of Community Organizing and Engagement, Cam Morris and the Community Organizing and Engagement team. RESPONSIBILITIES Embeds DEI and racial equity practices and tools into the everyday functioning of the Commission. Monitors and responds to the COE team email for questions, requests, and support needs. Supports team meeting planning, upcoming calendar coordination, and outreach preparation. Preps weekly all-staff updates, coordinates collaboration meetings, and other external meetings as assigned. Sends weekly/biweekly emails to external partners sharing updates and resources. Follow up with community partners on upcoming events and support cross-team collaboration. Support outreach to members for a monthly member highlight in the NYC CORE newsletter. Maintains the COE physical and OneDrive systems by creating an efficient storage process for all COE materials. Track social media feedback, survey responses, general community feedback, and public responses to share with the COE team. Track racial equity news on NYC CORE and mandated areas of focus. Plan logistics, attend external events with the COE team, and follow up with connections for future collaboration. Support with data collection/data entry during the Community Equity Priorities cycle engagement process. Attend outreach opportunities, team meetings, and other team-related tasks based on interests and team needs. Participate in special projects and complete other duties as assigned. About You Commitment to racial equity and seeking a values-aligned role that involves significant creativity and challenge. Community organizing and engagement or customer service experience. An understanding of racial equity, power, privilege, and oppression and how that shapes lived experiences. Some professional experience and at least 2 years of college completed. Background of living in, working within, or growing up as a member of communities facing historical oppression will contribute to your ability to guide the planning process. Demonstrated commitment, competency and strong familiarity with issues affecting Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, Middle Eastern, or Pacific Islander communities in New York City, or other marginalized groups. Demonstrated history of building relationships for your team to enable execution of a strategy that extends beyond the Office. Excellent time management skills and experience working in a deadline-driven environment. Some experience with technical skills, project support, or administrative skills is necessary. Final offers may vary from the amount listed based on candidate experience and expertise, and other factors. roles.title: Employee Experience Intern
roles.description: Our Purpose At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here. About Us SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters. Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity. What Are We Looking For? We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes. As an Employee Experience Intern you will help create a meaningful and engaging workplace for our employees through a blend of administrative support, program coordination, and creative projects. You’ll assist with onboarding logistics, benefits documentation, wellness initiatives, internal communications, and in-person events. The ideal candidate is organized, proactive, and passionate about building an inclusive and high-impact employee experience. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on exposure to multiple areas of HR, culture, and operations at a fast-growing tech company. What will you do? Onboarding • Support logistics, materials, and checklists for onboarding • Coordinate first-day experiences and gather feedback Benefits & Wellness • Organize and track benefit usage • Maintain internal benefits documentation • Research and suggest perk/wellness improvements Employee Experience & Engagement • Assist in planning in-person events and team activities • Support internal comms, celebrations, and culture initiatives HR Operations & Admin • Maintain records and systems • Help with documentation and internal process improvements Projects You Could Own or Support • Benefits overview guide • In-person events calendar • Employee experience touchpoint mapping • Pulse surveys and feedback reports What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring? • Bachelor’s or Master’s student in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, or related field • Strong organizational and project management skills • Creative and proactive in thinking about ways to enhance team culture • Excellent communication skills and attention to detail • A genuine interest in employee engagement, events, and wellness Why SentinelOne? AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place. We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family: SentinelOne is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. SentinelOne participates in the E-Verify Program for all U.S. based roles. To learn more about how we use AI in our hiring process, please review our AI in Hiring Candidate Disclosure .

roles.description: Employee Experience Program Support Intern Description - Before applying please note that, to be eligible for this position, you must be currently enrolled at a university in Spain, remain enrolled until the end of the internship, and be eligible to sign an internship agreement with your university. You must also be available to start the internship in February 2027 and continue participating in the program until June–July 2027. About HP and HP Barcelona HP creates technology that makes life better for everyone, everywhere. Operating in more than 170 countries, we bring together people with different backgrounds and perspectives to solve challenges and shape the future of work. HP Barcelona is a major research and development hub, with more than 800 engineers and over 150 inventions annually. As the global headquarters for HP’s Large Format Printing and 3D Printing business units, the site brings together expertise across software, firmware, and hardware. alongside engineering, our Sales, Operations, Marketing, Supply Chain, Customer Support, and Finance teams collaborate to improve customer experience and how we work. Join an inclusive, international workplace where you can be yourself, learn from experienced colleagues, and contribute your ideas. About Global Revenue Operations (GRO): GRO is part of Commercial Organization in HP and leads the stimulating digital transformation with the expected outcome to become a more experience-driven organization. It is a strategic function that helps drive HP’s Digital Transformation and Innovation in Sales processes, including our Channel Partners. GRO builds relationships with HP Customers, Partners as well as dedicated HP Sales Teams, understanding operational business models, identifying challenges in the operational process, and finding solutions on how to improve HP interlock in the operational environment. As part of GRO, the Strategy and Planning Team, drives standardized strategies, planning and execution processes across GRO. You will be part of a global team of highly engaged and capable colleagues supporting the organizational charter. The GRO Employee Experience Program Support - Intern will work alongside the Human Resources, Learning and Development, and Leadership teams to support the design, development, delivery, and evaluation of employee experience programs within GRO. These programs help employees feel empowered and develop agility, adaptability, and resilience. The intern will also help prepare program communications and improve how employee experience initiatives are shared across the organization. In this role, you will: Support the planning of training programs aligned with the organization’s employee experience roadmap. Help create and update training content and learning materials. Assist with program rollout by suggesting creative tools and methods to engage participants. Support program evaluation by helping track participation and gather feedback. Collect and review participant feedback to help improve training content and program structure. Help communicate training materials, available tools, and schedules to program participants. Learn about and support the organization’s employee experience priorities and roadmap. Requirements: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Administration / Management, or Marketing, and approaching graduation. Technical skills: Basic planning and project coordination skills, with an interest in learning and development, human resources, and improving employee experiences. Familiarity with project management and change management concepts is a plus. Soft skills: Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to explain complex topics clearly and work collaboratively. Good organization, creative problem solving, initiative, adaptability, integrity, and a positive attitude toward learning. Fluent in English, both spoken and written. Experience our benefits: Paid internship within a global, technology driven company. Join an international work environment, with opportunities for learning, professional development, and networking across teams. Flexible working schedule, with options for part-time agreements (4 hours/day) or full-time (8 hours/day). The length of the internship ranges from 4 to 12 months. Access to our intern community, including career development workshops, learning sessions, and social activities that help you grow professionally and connect with other interns. Mentor assigned. Opportunity to join the HP Graduate Program following the placement. Lunch at reduced prices at our canteen. Access to our on‑site sports center, including: Gym facilities Squash, tennis, and basketball courts 25+ organized sports and wellness activities, such as HIIT training, squash, basketball, and yoga Participation in the NextGen Employee Network, offering regular events and opportunities to connect with other early‑career professionals. On‑site medical services, including access to a doctor, nutrition support, physiotherapy, and general healthcare. Free printing access and hands‑on workshops using the latest HP technologies — from large‑format prints to 3D‑printed models. Easy commuting: Free parking available or excellent access via nearby train services. Women Network initiatives: Networking events, STEM promotion, business acumen talks, work–life balance sessions, and future‑skills development. We are looking for visionaries who are ready to make an impact on the way the world works. At HP, the future is yours to create. Sounds like you? Please apply and let’s talk! About Advocate Health Advocate Health is the third-largest nonprofit, integrated health system in the United States, created from the combination of Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health. Providing care under the names Advocate Health Care in Illinois; Atrium Health in the Carolinas, Georgia and Alabama; and Aurora Health Care in Wisconsin, Advocate Health is a national leader in clinical innovation, health outcomes, consumer experience and value-based care. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, Advocate Health services nearly 6 million patients and is engaged in hundreds of clinical trials and research studies, with Wake Forest University School of Medicine serving as the academic core of the enterprise. It is nationally recognized for its expertise in cardiology, neurosciences, oncology, pediatrics and rehabilitation, as well as organ transplants, burn treatments and specialized musculoskeletal programs. Advocate Health employs 155,000 teammates across 69 hospitals and over 1,000 care locations, and offers one of the nation’s largest graduate medical education programs with over 2,000 residents and fellows across more than 200 programs. Committed to providing equitable care for all, Advocate Health provides more than $6 billion in annual community benefits.

roles.title: Event Management Intern
roles.description: Are you obsessed with data, partner success, taking action, and changing the game? If you have a whole lot of hustle and a touch of nerd, come work with Pattern! We want you to use your skills to push one of the fastest-growing companies in the US to the top of the list. Pattern accelerates brands on global ecommerce marketplaces leveraging proprietary technology and AI. Utilizing more than 66 trillion data points, sophisticated machine learning and AI models, Pattern optimizes and automates all levers of ecommerce growth for global brands, including advertising, content management, logistics and fulfillment, pricing, forecasting and customer service. Hundreds of global brands depend on Pattern’s ecommerce acceleration platform every day to drive profitable revenue growth across 60+ global marketplaces—including Amazon, Walmart.com, Target.com, eBay, Tmall, TikTok Shop, JD, and Mercado Libre. To learn more, visit pattern.com or email press@pattern.com. Pattern has been named one of the fastest growing tech companies headquartered in North America by Deloitte and one of best-led companies by Inc. We place employee experience at the center of our business model and have been recognized as one of Newsweek’s Global Most Loved Workplaces®. Join Pattern’s marketing team to help execute Accelerate27, our largest event of the year, on April 19-21, 2027, along with our Q1 and Q2 field events. You must be available for the Accelerate dates to apply. At Accelerate, you’ll coordinate with sponsors, support on-site attendee trainings, and help deliver brand partner experiences. Beyond Accelerate, you’ll help plan sales events and experiences around the country, organize brand prospect data, book venues, and create a world-class attendee experience, with on-site logistics support as your schedule allows. Throughout, you’ll collaborate with our revenue and ecommerce teams. This is a part-time role initially (10-20 hours a week) from early January through the end of the semester, then full time through the end of April. You will work a hybrid schedule based in Lehi, Utah. What is a day in the life of an Event Marketing Intern? The Event Marketing Intern will support the Event Marketing team by assisting in planning and coordinating Accelerate27 and field events. This person will personally own a portion of Accelerate27 and fully plan and coordinate all details for day-of success In addition to owning a portion of the event, the intern will also support in several aspects of planning and on-site coordination, specifically regarding sponsor and brand partner experiences Assist on-site at events and learn how to think and act on the job during full-scale events Own an event-related Pattern project that builds knowledge of the ecommerce industry and helps advance Pattern’s marketing and sales growth Support the development and curation of additional event details for Accelerate and Pattern What will I need to thrive in this role? Must be a junior or senior in college enrolled in a degree in Experience Design and Management, Marketing, Event Marketing, or related field Superior interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Thrives in a fast paced environment with the ability to make quick decisions when needed Teachable and fast learner, but willing to slow down and ask questions when necessary High ethical standards Experience in ecommerce or digital-first brands or marketplace commercial efforts (D2C, Amazon, Walmart.com, etc.) is a plus Experience organizing and running events is a plus What does high performance look like? You have high attention to detail and exceptional organizational skills You give 100% to all tasks and projects you are given You will take full ownership of your projects and follow through to completion in a timely manner, while exercising transparency with your manager What is my potential for career growth? This role will introduce you to event marketing, specifically large scale events, and help you develop skills in event organizing, working with executives, researching and building out specific event details, and executing on-site at a high level Upon successful completion of this internship, you may be offered a full time position What is the team like? You will work with, and be mentored by, an Event Marketing Manager. You will meet with them on a regular basis to discuss your performance. This team is data driven and results oriented. You will collaborate regularly with members of your team to implement actionable solutions. Ideas and input are encouraged from all members.

roles.title: Extended Case Management Intern ( Spring2027)
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Scope of Work: The Extended Case Management (ECM) team provides case management services to up to 400 new clients each year at the IRC in Silver Spring. The team works directly with new refugees, asylees and other humanitarian immigrants resettling in the DC Metro area; utilizing a holistic 2Gen household approach for the families served, the team addresses both short-term and long-term barriers to support overall well-being in the US. This intern will report to one of the ECM caseworkers. Responsibilities: Conduct check-in calls and send messages to clients to determine the status of any unresolved service provision and provide guidance or assistance with the support of supervisor. Submit and follow up with a variety of external referrals, including for English classes, health screenings, and housing assistance programs. Assist clients with scheduling and teaching them how to navigate various organizations, such as public benefit offices or medical offices. Assist clients with completing and following up on applications for public benefits, Medicaid, childcare vouchers, social security cards, and more. Research and build community resources to fill any gaps in services. Provide clients with public transportation orientations in the field if needed.
