roles.description: Job Description Gang Prevention Education Specialist - Unpaid Intern JOB SUMMARY School/Community based Gang Prevention Education Specialist will provide prevention and education programs to 5th grade students and other community-based groups. Assists in program development, community education and resource development. Applicants must currently be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program in an accredited college or university in the field of Social Work, Sociology, Psychology, Criminal Justice, Elementary or Secondary Education, Communications, Library Sciences, social or behavioral sciences or other related fields. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS The following duties and responsibilities are intended to be representative of the work performed by the incumbent(s) in this position and are not all-inclusive. The omission of specific duties and responsibilities will not preclude it from the position. Applicants must be prepared to demonstrate the ability to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation. Provides specific prevention programming to 5th grade students in a group setting utilizing an evidence-based curriculum. Participates as a member of local gang reduction coordinating bodies Follows the Choose Gang Free (CGF) program structure and communicate effectively with the CGF members. Attends weekly team meetings/case staffing. Follows all Law Enforcement Bureau (LEB) policies and CGF Advocate Code of Ethics. Provides community and faculty gang education and prevention training Assists in program, community education and resource development. Participates in community-based educational events. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSA) Basic Knowledge of: Evidence-based practices. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy principles. Motivational Interviewing techniques Understanding of Moral Reconation Therapy (MRT) principles. Knowledge of the stages of moral development. Family dynamics. Juvenile Justice Process. What Works Principles, Risk-Needs-Responsivity model. Local gang issues, gang culture and how to identify gang signs, symbols, graffiti, colors, etc.. Skills and Abilities to: Ability to lead and manage group discussions/activities with children 9-11 years old. Network effectively with a variety of types of organizations, including government agencies, schools, social service agencies, law enforcement, courts/probations/corrections, grassroots organizations. Understand and explain factors leading to gang involvement, community dynamics and history Demonstrate organization, administration and personnel management skills Exercise judgment regarding appropriate confidentiality requirements Demonstrate organization, administration and personnel management skills Establish and maintain cooperative relationships with those contacted in the course of work Work independently under minimal supervision Meeting facilitation, conflict resolution, and consensus-building Work effectively with diverse populations Perform general office administrative activities: copying, filing, delivering and using the telephone and computers, including software. WORKING CONDITIONS AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Able to Lift up to 25 pounds occasionally and sit and work at a computer keyboard for extended periods of time. IMPORTANT INFORMATION REGARDING THIS POSITION This position is 15 hours a week, typically elementary school hours, 8:30-3:00. Teaching in one (1) to three (3) locations a week. Community based events are possible weekends or evenings as needed and we can be flexible with the weekly schedule.

roles.title: Global Public Affairs Intern – European & Nordic Policy (Early Careers)
roles.description: Are you studying political science, economics or business, and do you want to understand how politics, regulation and geopolitics shape one of the world’s largest integrated logistics companies? As Global Public Affairs Intern at Maersk, you will join our Europe team, with a particular focus on the Nordic countries, and work on live political issues alongside colleagues who advise senior management and engage with governments, authorities and industry organisations. Key Responsibilities As an intern in Global Public Affairs, you will work where Maersk’s business priorities meet politics, regulation and geopolitics. We support all parts of the business on political issues, and the team has a global remit. You will contribute to tasks such as: Monitoring and analysing political and legislative developments in the EU, Denmark, Sweden and the wider Nordic region, and assessing what they mean for Maersk’s business. Preparing briefs and background material for senior executives ahead of meetings with ministers, officials and other stakeholders. Conducting desk research and analysis on topics such as societal security and preparedness, critical infrastructure, supply chain resilience and trade policy. Contributing to positions and consultation responses on policy issues. Supporting the planning of stakeholder meetings, delegation visits, seminars and other external engagements. Taking on a defined project of your own during the internship, with responsibility for delivering it from start to finish. Join us in this exciting role where you will make a significant impact on Maersk’s global engagements and strategic initiatives, driving forward our mission to connect and simplify our customers’ supply chains while leading the way in sustainable practices. Why Choose Maersk? By joining Maersk, you’re becoming a part of a pioneering force in integrated logistics, dedicated to improving the quality of life of people by integrating the world. Our Global Public Affairs team is at the forefront of shaping the dialogue on global integration, leveraging our expansive network to champion initiatives that drive meaningful change. As an intern, you’ll gain unparalleled insights into the mechanics of global trade and the strategic considerations of a leading multinational and support our climate-journey towards net-zero. As Intern at Maersk, you will also become part of our international student network full of activities and events. Who We’re Searching For We are looking for a structured and detail-oriented student with a genuine interest in how business and politics interact. You are pursuing a master’s degree or are in the final year of your bachelor’s degree, in political science, economics, business or another relevant field at a Danish University based out of Copenhagen, Denmark. You: Can turn political and business issues into clear, concise analysis and written material. Work in a structured way and with strong attention to detail, also when deadlines are tight. Take ownership of your tasks and see them through to delivery. Speak and write Danish or Swedish at a professional level, and are fluent in English. Are proficient in PowerPoint and Excel. The internship is a full-time position (37 hours/week) at our Copenhagen headquarters from January to [June/July] 2027. We are, however, flexible to accommodate potential scheduling conflicts and your university credit transfer requirements. Maersk is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we embrace different styles of thinking. Maersk is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applicants without regard to race, colour, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy or parental leave, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with all legal requirements. We are happy to support your need for any adjustments during the application and hiring process. If you need special assistance or an accommodation to use our website, apply for a position, or to perform a job, please contact us by emailing accommodationrequests@maersk.com .

roles.title: Global Supply Management Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Global Supply Management Team The Global Supply Management Team ensures that Zipline has the parts it needs from suppliers around the world in a reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective way. We build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, negotiate contracts, and monitor supplier performance to reduce supply risk. The team also works closely with the design engineering, supplier industrial engineering, finance, program management, and material management teams to understand part design, manage supply against demand, drive cost reductions, and streamline logistics across international markets. The Role As a Global Supply Management Intern, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the systems, data, and supplier relationships that power Zipline’s global supply chain. You’ll work alongside supply managers, engineers, finance, and operations teams to support sourcing, analytics, and day-to-day execution. This role is perfect for a student to apply classroom knowledge to real-world challenges in procurement, logistics, and global operations. Your work will directly support Zipline’s mission to deliver essential goods and services across the world while building critical skills in supply chain management. What You'll Do Assist in tracking and analyzing supplier performance, purchase orders, and delivery timelines. Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations on supply chain metrics. Support sourcing activities by gathering quotes, conducting supplier research, and benchmarking costs. Work with internal stakeholders to troubleshoot supply issues and identify process improvements. Participate in supplier meetings and cross-functional discussions to gain exposure to real-world negotiations and decision-making. Document and standardize processes to help build scalable systems. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Economics, or a related field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable working with spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets). Curiosity and eagerness to learn about global supply chain operations in a fast-paced environment. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work on cross-functional projects. Organizational skills and attention to detail, with a willingness to dive into both strategic and tactical tasks. What Else You Should Know Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January 2027 to April/May 2027. The hourly rate for this internship is $37 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

roles.title: Government Affairs Intern
roles.description: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at one of our offices (Torrance/Idaho Falls/Washington D.C.) and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package if eligible. ABOUT THE ROLE Antares Nuclear is seeking a highly motivated and resourceful Government Affairs Intern to support the company's government affairs, communications, international business development, and commercial business development efforts from our Washington, D.C. office. This position offers a unique opportunity to work on emerging national security and energy policy issues while helping advance the commercialization and international deployment of next-generation nuclear technology. The intern will support research, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and business development initiatives, working closely with Antares leadership and cross-functional teams. The ideal candidate is an excellent writer and researcher, has a strong interest in national security, energy, public policy, or emerging technologies, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where initiative and attention to detail are essential. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: - Monitor congressional activity, federal legislation, appropriations, defense authorization, and executive branch initiatives relevant to advanced nuclear energy and microreactor deployment. - Research and analyze policy developments across the Pentagon, Department of Energy, Department of State, Department of Commerce, NASA, and other relevant federal agencies. - Assist in preparing briefing materials, talking points, policy memoranda, presentations, and other materials for meetings with government officials and congressional offices. - Track engagement with congressional offices, federal agencies, military services, and other key stakeholders. - Identify opportunities to advance policies, programs, and funding initiatives that support microreactor deployment for national security and commercial applications. - Support the development of strategic communications materials that articulate Antares’ mission, technology, and value proposition to government, commercial, and international audiences. - Draft and edit executive talking points, briefing materials, presentation content, website copy, and other communications products. - Monitor media coverage, industry developments, and public discourse related to advanced nuclear energy, national security, and microreactor deployment. - Help translate complex technical and policy issues into clear, accessible messages tailored to different audiences, including policymakers, prospective customers, strategic partners, and the general public. - Assist in developing communications strategies for key company milestones, government announcements, industry events, and strategic partnerships. - Identify opportunities to raise awareness of Antares’ work through relevant publications, industry forums, conferences, and other external channels. - Research international markets and identify countries, government agencies, utilities, defense organizations, and other prospective customers for Antares microreactors. - Assess country-level opportunities based on energy demand, national security priorities, regulatory frameworks, financing mechanisms, and government support for nuclear energy. - Support engagement with U.S. embassies, the State Department, the Foreign Commercial Service, international partners, and prospective overseas customers. - Research foreign government procurement processes, export requirements, financing options, and other factors affecting international reactor deployment. - Prepare country profiles, market assessments, customer briefings, and presentations to support Antares' international growth strategy. - Identify prospective commercial customers and strategic partners across sectors such as data centers, critical infrastructure, industrial facilities, remote power systems, and other energy-intensive applications. - Research customer power requirements, market dynamics, competing energy technologies, and potential use cases for microreactors. - Assist with developing customer presentations, market analyses, business cases, and strategic partnership proposals. - Maintain and update business development pipelines, stakeholder databases, and opportunity trackers. - Support preparation for customer meetings, industry conferences, and strategic partner engagements. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in public policy, international relations, political science, economics, business, engineering, energy policy, or a related field. - Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills. - Demonstrated interest in national security, energy, emerging technologies, international affairs, or commercial strategy. - Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise briefings and recommendations. - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. - Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word, and Excel. - A proactive, intellectually curious approach and willingness to take ownership of assignments. PREFERRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE: - Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to manage sensitive matters and competing priorities in a fast-moving environment. - Experience with congressional offices, federal agencies, think tanks, political campaigns, consulting, or business development. - Familiarity with U.S. national security policy, federal appropriations, international trade, or the energy sector. - Experience conducting market research, developing presentations, or preparing policy and business memoranda. - Foreign language proficiency or international experience. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: - Ability to travel as needed for government, regulator, supplier, customer, and international partner engagements. - Ability to support time-sensitive milestones or incidents outside standard business hours when necessary. LOCATION - We are located in downtown Washington, DC in a space designed for team collaboration and easy access to Capitol Hill, federal government offices, foreign embassies, and DC-based think tanks. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

In this role, you'll support the day-to-day work of the People team, build hands-on experience across the full employee lifecycle (onboarding, employee experience, HR operations, and programs). You’ll also support the day-to-day operations of our Boston office as part of creating a strong in-person employee experience. You'll partner closely with our People Ops, Talent Acquisition, and leadership teams, and you'll get exposure to how a fast-growing tech company runs its HR function in real time. This is a six-month, full-time co-op with regular exposure to senior People leaders. Please note we will only be considering applications from candidates currently enrolled in Northeastern University's co-op program and located within our Boston, MA hub. This is an in-person role (5 days a week) to support office operations and in-person employee experience. What you'll be doing: People & HR Coordination Support the People team across HRIS data entry, employee changes, and document management, helping maintain accurate and well-organized records Assist with scheduling interviews, coordinating reference checks, and supporting candidate experience throughout the hiring process Help maintain People team trackers, dashboards, and reporting on hiring, onboarding, and employee lifecycle metrics. Draft and proofread internal communications, FAQs, and People team documentation. Help monitor and respond to People team inquiries, answering common questions and routing requests with guidance Onboarding & Employee Experience Support logistics for new hire onboarding, including pre-boarding communications, equipment coordination, and Day 1 setup for Boston-based hires. Partner with IT and People Ops to make sure every new hire has a smooth, well-organized onboarding experience. Assist with employee experience programs (recognition, milestones, internal events), including planning, logistics and execution Support engagement survey logistics, including communications, response tracking, and follow-up coordination. Boston Office Management Support day-to-day operations of the Boston office, including supplies, snacks, mail, vendor relationships, and basic facilities needs. Assist with planning and executing Boston office events, team gatherings, and on-site experiences for visiting team members and executives. Coordinate with building management, security, and vendors to support office operations Partner with the People team to keep the office a welcoming, organized, and on-brand space that supports our hybrid work model. Programs & Projects Contribute to People team projects across areas such as Learning and Development, AI proficiency, performance, and culture initiatives. Help build process documentation, SOPs, and how-to guides that scale beyond your co-op term. What success looks like: Within your first 30 days, you’ve ramped on Later’s People tools and processes, built relationships with key stakeholders, and begun supporting onboarding, coordination, and leading office operations tasks. By 90 days, you’re confidently supporting core workflows (e.g., onboarding logistics, scheduling, and office coordination), contributing to People team projects, and helping manage day-to-day operations of the Boston office with guidance, while identifying opportunities to improve processes and the employee experience. By the end of your co-op term, you’ve gained hands-on experience across HR operations and employee experience, and contributed documentation or improvements that support the team after you leave. You’ll walk away with practical skills and a clear understanding of how a People team operates. What you bring: Currently enrolled at Northeastern University and eligible for a full-time, six-month co-op term. Coursework or interest in Human Resources, Organizational Behavior, Business, Communications, or a related field (or equivalent experience that signals readiness for HR work). Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with a high bar for professionalism when handling sensitive employee information. Comfortable with digital tools (Google Workspace, Slack, project trackers) and quick to pick up new systems like HRIS and ATS platforms. Available to work on-site at our Boston office five days per week to support office management responsibilities. Prior internship, co-op, or part-time experience in HR, People Operations, office management, or hospitality is a plus. Exposure to HRIS, ATS (Greenhouse), or workplace systems is a bonus, not a requirement. Interest in how AI tools are being used to scale HR and operations work. How you work: Driven by Impact: You deliver results that matter—prioritizing high-value work, meeting deadlines, and adapting quickly while keeping outcomes clear. Strategic & Customer-Centric: You anticipate risks and opportunities, connect decisions to long-term growth, and build trust through proactive insights. Curious & Growth-Oriented: You seek knowledge, ask sharp questions, and apply learnings fast—challenging the status quo with a mindset of improvement. Collaborative & Resilient: You thrive in change by staying resourceful, solution-focused, and positive—removing roadblocks, sharing insights, and keeping morale high. Accountable & Honest: You own your work, hold yourself and others to a high bar, and use transparent feedback to drive growth. Emotionally Intelligent: You build trust through empathy and collaboration, foster inclusion, and inspire others with grit, optimism, and integrity. Our approach to compensation: We take a market-based & data-driven approach to compensation. We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation bi-annually, including performance and market-related factors. Our salaries are benchmarked against market Total Cash Compensation for the geographic location of our job posting. Compensation for some roles is structured as On Target Earnings (OTE = base + commission/variable) while for others it is structured as Salary only. roles.title: Human Factors (Winter Co-Op)
roles.description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW: A seaglider floats, foils, and flies — and every one of those transitions has to make sense to the pilots flying it and the passengers riding in it. Nobody has designed that interface before. As a Human Factors Co-Op, you’ll help shape it: contributing to concept sketches, UI/UX standards, and the usability evaluations that keep the interface safe, intuitive, and ready for certification. As part of the Systems team, you’ll be joining a group of driven, collaborative, and talented engineers who take pride in solving complex technical challenges and making an impact as a team. We hold a high bar for engineering rigor, move quickly, think boldly, and rely on our teamwork to push boundaries and bring entirely new technology into the world. If you’d rather sketch and test a real interface than read about one, and you want hands-on experience on a vehicle nobody has built before, we’d love to have you on the team! What You'll Do: - Contribute to new feature concepts. Bring ideas for how pilots and passengers interact with the seaglider human interface. - Help build out our design standards. Contribute to REGENT’s UI/UX standards and design language. - Support safety and usability evaluations. Help plan and run evaluations of the seaglider human interface. - Help define human factors requirements. Support requirements definition and draft test procedures. - Partner across engineering disciplines. Work with engineers across systems, software, and flight test to bring HF findings into the design. What We’re Looking For: - Working toward a relevant degree. Pursuing a degree in Human Factors Engineering, Engineering Psychology, or a related field. - Some exposure to aviation or maritime contexts. Coursework, research, or personal flying, boating, or sailing experience. - Comfort with prototyping and communication. Proficiency with rapid prototyping tools (e.g., Figma); excellent written and verbal communication, including technical documentation. - Self-motivated and adaptable. Comfortable with shifting priorities in a startup environment. Who We’re Looking For: - Curious about people, not just tech. You want to know why someone struggles with an interface, not just that they do, and you’re excited to go find out firsthand. - Hands-on, not just theoretical. You’d rather sketch a quick mockup or run a small usability test than write a memo about what one might find. - Comfortable without a precedent. A seaglider cockpit doesn’t look like anything that exists yet. You’re energized by that, not looking for a template to follow. - Present for the work. Evaluations and test days don’t always land on a tidy schedule, and you’re ready to show up when the work needs you. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

roles.description: At First Student, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are seeking a motivated, creative, and detail-oriented HR & Marketing Communications Intern to support employee experience, retention, engagement, recognition, and internal communications initiatives that help inform, connect, and celebrate our teams. This internship is a great opportunity for a student or early-career professional who wants to learn how Human Resources and Marketing Communications work together to support employees across a large, purpose-driven organization. The intern will gain hands-on experience assisting with HR programs, communication planning, content creation, project coordination, and employee-facing materials while working closely with HR and communications partners. Key Responsibilities Human Resources Support Support employee experience initiatives focused on engagement, retention, recognition, connection, and belonging. Assist with HR programs, events, meetings, project timelines, and follow-up activities that support our employees and leaders. Help prepare employee-facing resources, guides, FAQs, toolkits, and communications that are clear, practical, and easy to use. Research HR best practices, employee engagement trends, and communication approaches that support a strong team culture. Assist with organizing survey feedback, participation data, recognition updates, or other HR program information to support action planning and continuous improvement. Maintain organized project files, trackers, and documentation to help HR programs run smoothly and on time. Marketing Communications Support Draft, edit, and proofread internal communications, newsletters, announcements, leader messages, and employee updates that are clear, engaging, and aligned to First Student’s voice. Support content development for digital channels, employee communication platforms, presentations, campaign materials, and recognition communications. Help create audience-friendly messaging that connects employees to HR programs, company updates, and opportunities to share their voice. Partner with HR and Marketing Communications team members to gather information, organize content, and shape key messages for employee audiences. Assist with basic design or layout support for flyers, one-pagers, PowerPoint slides, and communication assets that are simple, visual, and easy to understand. Track communication requests, deadlines, approvals, and distribution needs to help ensure timely delivery. Bring creative ideas that help improve employee awareness, participation, and engagement in HR programs and communications. Qualifications Currently pursuing a degree in Human Resources, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Business, or a related field. Strong writing, editing, proofreading, and verbal communication skills with the ability to make information clear and employee-friendly. Comfortable using Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, and Teams; experience with Canva or similar design tools is a plus. Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Creative, curious, dependable, and willing to learn in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment. Ability to handle information professionally and maintain confidentiality when supporting HR-related work. Positive attitude, service mindset, and interest in employee engagement, workplace culture, and communications that support frontline and office-based teams. What the Intern Will Gain Hands-on experience supporting HR, employee experience, and internal communications initiatives in a large, service-focused organization. Exposure to employee engagement, retention, recognition, onboarding, change communication, and program support strategies. Opportunities to strengthen business writing, content planning, project coordination, presentation, and communication skills. Experience collaborating with cross-functional partners and learning how clear communication supports employees, leaders, and business goals. A practical understanding of how HR programs are communicated, measured, improved, and brought to life for employees. Work Environment This internship offers a hybrid work schedule with flexibility to work both remotely and in person at our downtown office location. The intern should be available to come into the office as needed for collaboration, meetings, onboarding, project work, and team connection. Free parking is available for in-office days. roles.title: Intensive Case Management Intern
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. NOTE ABOUT COMPENSATION: Internships at the IRC are unpaid. No financial compensation, including compensation for relocation, is available. Reimbursement is available for mileage when using a personal vehicle. Eligible interns will also receive a nominal per diem reimbursement aligned with current intern reimbursement policies. BACKGROUND: The International Rescue Committee (IRC), established in 1933, is a prominent non-profit organization dedicated to assisting refugees and those affected by oppression or violent conflict. Providing a wide range of services, the IRC focuses on emergency relief, protection, rehabilitation, resettlement, and advocacy for vulnerable populations. Within the United States, the organization operates 28 offices that support newly arrived individuals by ensuring they have access to essential resources such as food, shelter, and clothing, while also working with refugees to help them achieve self-sufficiency. SCOPE OF INTERN WORK: The intensive case management (ICM) program offers essential support to our most vulnerable refugee clients, guiding clients on their journey to self-sufficiency during their crucial first years in the U.S. ICM clients include single parent families, LGBTQ+, survivors of domestic violence, and clients with complex medical and mental health needs. Our services include comprehensive assistance in health, employment, finances, DWS, education, housing, family, and community integration. As a casework intern, you will collaborate closely with experienced ICM caseworkers, gaining valuable insights and hands-on experience in all facets of our impactful casework program. MINIMUM COMMITMENT: 15 – 20 hours per week for 10-12 weeks START DATE: January 12, 2027 (final start date to be confirmed) RESPONSIBILITIES: Shadowing caseworkers and completing relevant core service delivery trainings. Assisting clients one-on-one with core services, including but not limited to: Benefits applications Bus and grocery store orientations Job search and applications Delivering food and in-kind donation items Personal finance and bill payment Transportation to appointments Medical insurance navigation Home visits Client relocations Referring and connecting clients to community services Assisting walk-in clients, as needed. Supporting caseworkers in data compliance, including case filing, case noting, data entry, and tracking. Participation in weekly casework team meetings. Other relevant duties as assigned. LEARNING OBJECTIVES: Understand how state and federal policies affect services to clients. Experience working with diverse populations. Learn the social work interventions/models used at the agency and will practice applying social work theories/approaches to cases (strengths, empowerment, ecological, systems, etc.). Learn how to navigate and understand social benefits and resources available in our Utah communities. REQUIREMENTS: Must be currently enrolled in a graduate/undergraduate program, or have graduated less than 6 months ago. Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in English; fluency in additional language(s) preferred. Background in social work OR other related fields. Experience working with refugees/diverse populations, elderly, domestic violence survivors, of people with disabilities. Motivated, flexible and ability to work independently, prioritize, and manage time effectively. Strong computer skill with proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and Outlook). Demonstrated ability to communicate and work as a team member in a cross-cultural environment. Complete IRC background check & all related orientations/trainings. IRC leading the way from harm to home. Equal Opportunity Employer: We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us at volunteerSLC@rescue.org to request any needed accommodation. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients. Cookies: https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. roles.title: Internship: Corporate Advocacy
roles.description: ABOUT NCOSE & INTERNSHIP PROGRAM: The National Center on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE) exists because people should be free to live and love without sexual abuse and exploitation! If you share this vision and want to help create a culture where all individuals can thrive, then we invite you to join us! The Exploitation Prevention & Advocacy program enables you to participate in the ongoing work of defending human dignity. Internships offer a unique opportunity to combat sexual abuse and exploitation while gaining new skills through hands-on opportunities that seek to prevent exploitation before it begins. Interns also enjoy abundant opportunities to meet nationally recognized leaders in the field of anti-sexual exploitation and attend education briefings. The program also offers interns an opportunity to investigate their individual strengths and develop new skills. NCOSE is focused on mass-scale prevention of sexual abuse and exploitation and deploys the tactics of corporate advocacy, public policy, civil litigation, and grassroots mobilization to reach this. Read about some of our recent victories here. ABOUT THIS POSITION: Mainstream corporations often facilitate, normalize, or even profit from various forms of sexual abuse and exploitation. NCOSE’s annual Dirty Dozen List—a powerful campaign which brings accountability to the mainstream corporate players in America which are perpetuating sexual exploitation—shines light on poor business policies and practices as well as crediting good actions in order to spark further corporate social responsibility and drive the formation of industry-wide safety standards. We utilize grassroots campaigns, evidence collection, storytelling, and coalition building to change policies in the private sector. Interns play a vital role in assisting with this work. *Applications for this position will be processed on a rolling basis, so interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible. *We are typically inundated with applications. We greatly appreciate your patience as we carefully review each candidate and ask that you hold your questions until contacted for an interview. TERM : January 6,- April 16, 2027; possible extension: six months or 1 year RESPONSIBILITIES WILL INCLUDE*: Support the interim-Director of Corporate Advocacy, including: Research corporate policies Collect evidence of policy violations, specifically regarding sexual exploitation and abuse of adults and minors Draft briefing documents and talking points When appropriate, attend meetings with corporate representatives and/or allies; take notes and assist with follow-up Follow current developments on relevant corporate and thematic issue areas; draft fact sheets, white papers, presentations, and synopses using media and academic resources relating to: online child safety; harms of pornography; harms of prostitution and other forms of commercial sex; demand for commercial sex and male sex buying behavior; organizations promoting, distributing, and/or profiting from sexual exploitation (pornography, stripping, prostitution, sexual assault, risky sexy behavior); sex trafficking of men, women and children. Report on social media trends and possible negative impacts and risks to minors Help conduct social media campaigns to advance advocacy efforts; Write blogs on sexual exploitation issues and NCOSE projects; Help organize and implement NCOSE meetings and events; take notes, and report out on internal and external meetings, webinars, etc. as directed. Assist as needed with office management including data entry (e.g. contact information of allies), answering of telephones, responding to email or other written requests, drafting correspondence, and filing. *Tasks may shift based on the organization’s current need and opportunities. QUALIFICATIONS : Passionate about opposing sexual exploitation, as well as a passion for NCOSE’s mission, vision and values University student or young professional Strong writing and communication skills.· Strong writing and communication skills· Strong organization skills and attention to detail are essential· Independent worker- must be able to complete tasks without constant management· Proficiency with basic Microsoft Office applications; mail merge, formatting letters data management in Excel, etc. Knowledge of the web and digital marketing techniques Has and can bring a working laptop and charger Ability to handle multiple tasks Experience conducting research and synthesizing information BENEFITS : Hands-on work with passionate, talented team members Mentorship from some of the movement’s kindest and most passionate leaders In-depth 12-week training on various exploitation issues Incredible networking opportunities with movement leaders A creative, collaborative, and inclusive company culture Opportunities to develop professionally and uncover skills you didn’t know you had Real-life experiences that will provide you with the confidence to delve into your next adventure COMPENSATION : NCOSE internships are unpaid. SCHEDULE: This position requires 24-40 hours per week. Candidates must be mostly available during NCOSE’s office hours of Monday through Friday 9:00am to 5:00pm EST in order to coordinate with the team. Our team is in the office on M, W, & Th and remote on T & F. Evenings and weekends are typically not eligible for a NCOSE internship. LOCATION : This internship is at NCOSE’s office headquarters in Washington, DC. The best experience is achieved in the office, where events, meetings, and opportunities for learning and networking happen regularly. Remote positions may be considered for outstanding applicants. TO APPLY : To apply, submit the checklist items and complete the questionnaire. · Cover Letter describing your interest in a NCOSE Internship · Resume · Two Letters of Reference · Unofficial Transcript · Writing Sample Incomplete applications, including those without reference letters, will not be considered. ---------------------------------------- About the National Center on Sexual Exploitation Please visit our About Page to learn more. You can find impact reports from previous years here .

roles.title: IRC Wichita Policy Intern Spring 2027
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. BACKGROUND: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. At work in over 50 countries and 28 US cities to restore safety, dignity, and hope, the IRC leads the way from harm to home. Domestically, our 28 offices across the US ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency. SCOPE OF WORK: This internship offers an excellent opportunity for a current undergraduate or graduate student, or recent graduate, to gain hands-on experience in public policy, research, and advocacy within an international humanitarian organization. The Policy Intern will support the IRC's efforts to understand policy developments affecting refugees, immigrants, and other displaced populations, with a particular focus on issues relevant to Kansas and the broader region. Working closely with IRC staff, the Policy Intern will conduct policy research, monitor legislative and regulatory developments, analyze relevant policies, prepare written materials, and support community engagement and advocacy initiatives. The intern will contribute to efforts to strengthen the organization's understanding of the policy landscape and communicate how policy decisions affect the communities IRC serves. RESPONSIBILITIES: • Policy Research and Analysis: Research federal, state, and local policies affecting refugees, immigrants, and other newcomer populations, including resettlement, health care access, employment, education, housing, and integration services. • Legislative Tracking: Monitor legislative proposals, regulatory changes, executive actions, and other policy developments relevant to IRC programs and the communities it serves. • Policy Briefs and Reports: Assist in drafting policy briefs, background memos, issue summaries, talking points, and reports to communicate key findings and inform organizational priorities. • Data Collection and Analysis: Collect and organize quantitative and qualitative information to support policy research, identify emerging trends, and assess the potential impact of policy changes on newcomer communities. • Stakeholder and Community Engagement: Research relevant policymakers, government agencies, advocacy organizations, and community partners to identify opportunities for collaboration and information sharing. • Advocacy Support: Assist with preparing materials for policy meetings, community briefings, stakeholder convenings, and advocacy initiatives, as appropriate. • Policy Landscape Mapping: Identify existing policies, programs, and resources that affect refugee and immigrant integration in Kansas and the surrounding region. • Internal Coordination: Collaborate with IRC staff across programs to gather information, understand community needs, and connect policy developments with the organization's direct service work. • Additional Projects: Provide support for other policy, research, and advocacy initiatives as needed and as feasible. LEARNING OBJECTIVES: • Gain practical experience in public policy research, legislative monitoring, and policy analysis within a nonprofit and humanitarian organization. • Develop an understanding of federal, state, and local policy processes and how policy decisions influence refugee resettlement, immigration, and newcomer integration. • Strengthen research, critical thinking, data interpretation, and professional writing skills through the development of policy briefs, reports, and other written materials. • Learn how nonprofit organizations engage with policymakers, government agencies, community partners, and advocacy networks. • Develop an understanding of the relationship between public policy, direct service delivery, and the needs of refugee and immigrant communities. • Gain exposure to the policy challenges and opportunities affecting IRC Resettlement, Asylum, and Integration programming. • Build skills in stakeholder research, policy communication, and evidence-based decision-making. REQUIREMENTS: • Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree, or a recent graduate. • Students pursuing degrees in public policy, political science, public administration, public health, international relations, sociology, economics, nonprofit management, or related fields are encouraged to apply. • Strong research, analytical, and critical-thinking skills. • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple assignments. • Ability to synthesize information from multiple sources and communicate findings clearly and concisely. • Familiarity with Microsoft Office programs, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. • Interest in immigration, refugee resettlement, humanitarian assistance, social services, or public policy. • Ability to work independently, collaborate effectively with a team, and seek guidance when needed. • Commitment to the IRC's mission and the principles of dignity, inclusion, and equitable access to opportunity Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. roles.title: Learning Community Experience Intern
roles.description: Do you enjoy building vibrant communities where people feel supported, motivated, and empowered to succeed? Are you passionate about learner engagement, retention, and creating inclusive environments that help individuals thrive? Are you proactive, organized, and comfortable working with both data and people to drive meaningful impact? Are you intrigued by the opportunity to help build and strengthen one of Africa’s most dynamic tech learning communities? If so, this might be the role for you. About ALX Africa ALX Africa, a non-profit organisation under the ALX Foundation, is dedicated to unlocking the potential of Africa's digital future. Formerly part of Sand Tech Holdings, we've embarked on an independent journey to provide world-class tech skills training and career acceleration programmes. Our mission is to bridge the digital divide, upskill and re-skill talent, and create a generation of innovative leaders. By 2030, we aim to empower 2 million Africans to secure sustainable tech careers. With hubs in 8 cities across Africa and counting, we provide safe access to quality learning and a dedicated network of expert instructors. Our innovative programmes equip learners with the practical skills and knowledge needed to succeed in today's rapidly evolving tech industry. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, industry partnerships, and hands-on projects, we prepare our students for in-demand roles in software engineering, data science, and cybersecurity. We achieve this by: Providing young professionals with access to the most in-demand tech skills that will power the future. Empowering the next generation of technology innovators, entrepreneurs, and business leaders through challenging, real-world coursework. Building a lifelong, impactful community of tech professionals that support them at all stages of their career journey. Our impact thus far: 205k+ learners since 2021 117k youth in work 13k youth starting own ventures 66k youth in jobs through entrepreneurship Visit our website www.alxafrica.com to learn more about our digital revolution. Role Summary The Learning Community Experience Intern will support the Learning Community Experience (LCE) function in strengthening learner engagement, participation, and retention within both physical hub spaces and virtual platforms. This role focuses on improving learner activation, supporting at-risk learners, coordinating engagement activities, and ensuring clear communication across the learner journey. The intern will play a key role in helping build a structured, inclusive, and high-participation learning environment that drives consistency and success. Specific Responsibilities Community Engagement & Participation Support the design and execution of engagement initiatives to increase participation at the hub and across digital platforms. Assist in planning and delivering community events such as workshops, AMAs, study halls, peer learning sessions, and onboarding activations. Drive attendance through structured promotion, reminders, and follow-ups. Help maintain a welcoming, inclusive, and learner-centered hub environment. Learner Support & Retention Support in identifying learners who may be at risk of disengagement and help provide simple intervention efforts. Provide timely and professional responses to learner inquiries. Assist with onboarding and integration of new learners into the community. Support peer mentorship and accountability initiatives. Communication & Coordination Execute communication plans across WhatsApp, email, and other community platforms. Ensure clear and consistent messaging regarding events, deadlines, and support opportunities. Support cross-functional coordination between learners, mentors, coordinators, and internal teams. Escalate learner concerns appropriately when required. Feedback & Continuous Improvement Collect and organize learner feedback through surveys, polls, and check-ins. Track participation metrics and support reporting. Analyze basic engagement data to identify trends and improvement opportunities. Contribute actionable ideas to enhance the learner experience. Community Growth & Advocacy Support identification and activation of learner ambassadors or community champions. Encourage ownership and active participation within the hub. Stay informed on community engagement best practices and contribute to improvements. Skill Requirements - Essential Bachelor’s degree (completed or in progress) in Communications, Marketing, Education, Social Sciences, or related field. Experience supporting student groups, communities, events, or engagement initiatives. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to engage respectfully with diverse groups. Strong organizational and time-management skills. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Basic data literacy (ability to track attendance, participation, and simple engagement metrics). Proficiency in Google Workspace tools (Docs, Sheets, Slides). Skill Requirements - Preferable Familiarity with e-learning platforms or digital community tools. Experience supporting retention or learner success initiatives. Experience coordinating events or managing small projects. Exposure to community management, student engagement, or education operations environments. Person Specification/Attributes Courage: Willingness to speak up, challenge the status quo, and embrace new challenges. Humility: Openness to learning, seeking help when needed, and a focus on serving others. Adventure: A passion for setting ambitious goals, tackling difficult tasks, and finding joy in the journey. Initiative: Proactive problem-solving, a sense of ownership, and a willingness to go above and beyond. Resilience: The ability to bounce back from setbacks, persevere through challenges, and emerge stronger. Empathetic yet structured. Detail-oriented with strong follow-through. Comfortable engaging both physically and virtually. Proactive problem-solver. Employment Type Full-time internship position Location Requirement As this is an in-person role, the candidate is required to be based in Accra, Ghana. Due to the considerable amount of virtual working and interaction with colleagues and customers in different physical locations internationally, it is essential that the successful applicant has the drive and ethic to succeed working in small teams physically but in larger efforts virtually. Self-drive to communicate constantly using web collaboration and video conferencing is essential. As an employee, you will be encouraged to continually develop your capability & attain certifications to reflect your growth as an individual.

roles.title: Marsh Risk Early Career Program, Summer Intern 2027 – Claims Advocacy, Chicago
roles.description: Company: Marsh Description: Special note: This position may close once a sufficient applicant pool has been reached, so interested candidates are encouraged to apply early. Marsh Risk Early Career Program, Summer Intern 2027 – Claims Advocacy, Chicago We are seeking talented individuals to join our Marsh Early Career Program Summer Internship , part of our Risk business at Marsh, within the Claims Advocacy team. This role will be based in Chicago with an anticipated start in June 2027. This is a hybrid role that has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office. Join Marsh's Early Career Program as a Summer Intern, a 10-week experience where interns will work directly with experts gaining exposure to a variety of claim advocacy disciplines, including workers' compensation, auto liability, general liability/products liability, environmental, product recall, and property claims. As part of our program benefits, you will have a vibrant cohort community and dedicated program team to provide learning and development opportunities, a mentorship program, exposure to senior leaders, and valuable networking opportunities. You’ll end your internship with a summer capstone presentation, giving you the opportunity to apply what you’ve learned and present your work to your team and senior leadership. The Team The Marsh Claims Advocacy Practice is comprised of a global team of experienced professionals, who are guided by the following key principles: Our Vision - Is to deliver claims excellence, using our extensive global network to produce integrated solutions for Clients. Our Approach - Is to tailor these solutions according to Client need and deliver them locally to provide a personal service. Our Objective - Is to add real value to Clients, particularly at times of their greatest need. High-performing graduating students may be considered for a full-time opportunity after the internship. We will count on you to: Support the team with the reporting, tracking, and documentation of client claims, helping ensure information is accurate and organized throughout the claims process. Assist with formal claim reviews by gathering and analyzing information, preparing supporting materials, and helping the team identify trends and insights that support clients and their risk. Collaborate with colleagues to support client needs, including preparing materials and coordinating information and follow-up with clients and other stakeholders. Assist with research, data analysis, presentations, and other projects that help the team evaluate claim activity. What you need to have: Graduation date between Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 Currently pursuing a bachelor degree in Business Administration, Risk Management, Marketing, Analytics or a related major Interest in claims, insurance, risk management, or learning how organizations respond to and manage risk Organized and detailed-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities Strong written and verbal communication skills, comfort collaborating with teammates Legal work authorization to work in the U.S on a permanent and ongoing basis without the need for sponsorship now or in the future, in other words, you must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident Green Card holder at the time of application What makes you stand out? Previous internship, work, or extracurricular experiences involving customer service or collaboration with others Comfortable working with data or spreadsheets and an interest in developing analytical skills Client-focused mindset with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders Application Process and Document Requirements Uploading Resume and Cover Letter (both required): We review applications holistically and value a wide range of academic, professional, and extracurricular experiences. Please upload documents that are no more than two pages each in PDF format. To ensure your application is considered complete, please submit a cover letter answering the questions below. We encourage thoughtful, authentic responses that reflect your interests, experiences, and alignment with Marsh. What interests you in beginning your career at Marsh within Claims Advocacy? Elaborate on why the city of Chicago appeals to you. Marsh works with clients and colleagues from diverse industries and backgrounds. Share an experience where you worked with people different from yourself and explain the importance of this in client-focused professional services. Compensation and Benefits The hourly rate for this role is $26/hr. in Chicago. Please note that the salary is standardized per location and not subject to negotiation. In addition, we offer: Mentorship and professional development support Hybrid work environment, offering a mix of in-office collaboration and remote flexibility Opportunities to participate in local office events and networking activities Why join our team: We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work, and supportive leaders. We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have an impact on colleagues, clients and communities. Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being. Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X. Marsh is committed to embracing a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, veteran status (including protected veterans), or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you have a need that requires accommodation, please let us know by contacting reasonableaccommodations@marsh.com. Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

roles.title: Operations Intern, Talent Development & Training
roles.description: Operations Intern, Talent Development & Training Hillel International Role Overview The Talent Development & Training team is seeking a highly organized, proactive, and collaborative Talent Development Operations Intern to ensure the seamless execution of HillelU’s growing portfolio of professional development programs and experiences. HillelU provides learning and development opportunities to more than 1,200 Hillel professionals across the organization. As our portfolio continues to grow, this role will provide the operational support needed to deliver high-quality professional development experiences consistently and efficiently—from virtual training and cohort programs to immersive in-person leadership development experiences. This role will serve as a key member of the Talent Development & Training team, taking ownership of the systems, logistics, data, and processes that support the participant experience. The ideal candidate is someone who loves turning plans into action, can anticipate details before they become problems, and is energized by making complex programs feel seamless. What You’ll Do Program Operations & Delivery Support the operational execution of assigned HillelU programs and learning experiences, from initial planning through post-program follow-up. Coordinate session setup, registration, materials, technology, and other operational needs. Manage pre- and post-program communications, including reminders, pre-work, and logistics. Provide or coordinate day-of technology and administrative support for virtual and in-person programs. Partner with facilitators and Talent Development colleagues to ensure they have the information and support needed for successful program delivery. Create and maintain repeatable processes, templates, and checklists that make program delivery more efficient and consistent. Identify operational challenges and proactively develop solutions. Program Data, Evaluation & Reporting Collect, organize, maintain and report on participation and program data. Pull and upload data across relevant systems and ensure program records remain accurate and up to date. Coordinate post-program evaluation processes, including evaluation communications and data collection. Develop regular reports and dashboards that help the Talent Development team understand participation, engagement, and program outcomes. Support analysis of program data to identify trends and inform future planning and decision-making. Partner with colleagues to improve how HillelU tracks and communicates program impact. Leadership Development & Event Logistics Support the operational delivery of select high-touch programs and experiences, including Kaplan Supervisory Leadership Program and Accelerate. Coordinate event logistics including hotels, catering, travel, participant communications, materials, schedules, and other event needs. Manage participant travel reimbursements and other program-related expenses. Coordinate across facilitators, participants, vendors, internal partners, and other stakeholders to ensure a seamless experience. Provide on-site operational support for select HillelU professional development experiences, as needed. Systems & Process Improvement Maintain systems for tracking HillelU programs, participants, logistics, and outcomes. Look for opportunities to streamline administrative processes and reduce manual work. Create documentation and standard operating procedures to support consistency and continuity across the HillelU portfolio. Help the team leverage technology and data more effectively in the delivery and evaluation of learning programs. Support implementation of new tools, systems, and processes as HillelU continues to evolve. Team Partnership Serve as a collaborative operational partner to Talent Development colleagues, helping translate program ideas into executable plans. Support multiple concurrent projects and priorities while maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Provide visibility into project status, upcoming deadlines, and operational needs. Take ownership of projects and follow through independently while knowing when to escalate questions or challenges. Contribute to a collaborative, positive, and service-oriented team culture. Who You Are Highly organized and detail-oriented , with the ability to manage many moving pieces without losing sight of the big picture. A strong project manager who can establish timelines, track details, and ensure work moves forward. Proactive and solutions-oriented , with a natural instinct to anticipate needs and troubleshoot challenges. A strong communicator who can build relationships and communicate clearly with a wide range of stakeholders. Comfortable with technology and data , and excited to learn new systems and tools. Service-oriented , with a strong commitment to creating excellent experiences for participants, facilitators, and colleagues. Able to work independently , take ownership, and exercise good judgment. Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple simultaneous priorities. Proficient in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce, Zoom, learning management systems, event platforms, or similar tools is a plus. We encourage both current college students and recent graduates to apply for this role. What You’ll Receive $17/hr up to 20 hours/week In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience in program operations, project coordination, data and evaluation, event logistics, and talent development while working alongside a team that designs and delivers professional development for Hillel professionals across the organization. You’ll have the opportunity to see how learning experiences are designed, delivered, evaluated, and improved and to build skills that translate across nonprofit, education, Human Resources, and business environments. About Hillel International In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.
